findings.text: Public wait helper for a migration entry at an address within an address space. It observes the table entry under protection and sleeps only while migration is still indicated, otherwise it releases protection and returns promptly.

Public wait helper for a migration entry held at middle level scope. It inspects the middle level descriptor under its dedicated lock and sleeps only while migration remains indicated, otherwise it unlocks and returns.
Public translation from a normal mapping page at an address to its enclosing folio. Absence of a normal page yields absence of a folio, so callers handle a null outcome.

Public predicate reporting whether a shared writable area needs dirty tracking. Tracking is required when filesystem operations request write notification or when the backing store supports writeback.
Public predicate identifying a secret memory area by equality of its operations vector with the dedicated secret memory vector.

Public lookup of the area covering or following a given address. One configuration searches an ordered tree with the address space lock asserted, while the configuration without memory management walks through an iterator positioned at the address.
Header helper exposing the current area of an iterator. It performs the walk itself and assumes any required locking is held by the caller.

Fault entry for a marker preserved in place of a normal translation. It rejects an empty marker, gives poisoning precedence over other handling, treats a guard marker as fatal, delegates write protection markers for userfault to dedicated handling, and rejects any other marker value.

Fault handling for read write protection traps from userfault. Synchronous mode reports to the handler, while asynchronous mode resolves inside the kernel only for a stable entry across lock acquisition, yielding default area protections without the trap marker, with youth indicated and writability decided by area upgrade policy.

Fault handling for balancing across memory nodes. It requires entry stability across table lock acquisition before any use, evaluates writability under that lock from current protections plus area upgrade policy, skips migration for absent or device associated folios, and otherwise may isolate and migrate with accounting of success or failure before restoring mappings.

A translation is eligible for a writable upgrade only when the area advertises write capability and the entry remains readable and neither soft dirty tracking nor userfault write tracking demands a fault.

Private upgrades additionally require association with a normal page in the exclusive anonymous class, matching the ability of the fault path to upgrade without further checks while holding the table lock.
Shared upgrades additionally require a dirty indication, interpreted as prior filesystem notification. A clean indication preserves the need for a notifying fault.

Swap cache release is refused without cache membership. Synchronous devices always release, as do full swap control groups and locked mappings or folios. Otherwise release requires both write fault direction and exclusive ownership.

Large swap in order selection has an always empty configuration. The selective configuration also reports none when per page fidelity is needed for userfault or when compressed swap has ever been enabled, otherwise it narrows enabled orders below middle level scope by area policy and address placement and swap alignment before range verification.

A candidate large swap in range is acceptable only when every entry in the aligned span continues the faulting swap offset without backend mixing, and when virtual and swap alignment agree on the candidate size. Only orders meeting those range properties are retained.
Exclusive swap handling assumes each entry in the span has a single remaining reference while table and folio locks stabilize the count. Violation is treated as a developer warning tied to the folio.

Mapping restoration after balancing returns entries to default area protections with youth indicated and writability as decided by the caller. Large folio restoration stays within the intersection of folio span and table span and area bounds, skips entries that are absent or accessible or belong to another folio, and preserves read write protection traps when that tracking is armed.

Fault direction flags are validated against area capabilities. Unsharing applies only to copy on write areas and is otherwise dropped, write direction requires write allowance with either write access or copy on write identity, and per area locking is incompatible with no wait retry semantics. Violations request segmentation termination.

Long term pinning with write intent is allowed unless dirty tracking is needed. Tracking is needed only for shared writable areas whose filesystem needs write notification or whose backing store supports writeback. Other pin combinations impose no restriction.

Direct page access permission checks reject device and frame map areas and secret memory, enforce anonymous only and filesystem direct access and huge page splitting constraints, require readable or writable capability with force fallback tied to copy on write identity, and finally defer to architecture access permission.

Address to area lookup for direct page access never grows stacks. A downward growing area with a nearby miss below its start triggers a rate limited warning and yields no area, while other misses directly yield absence or the located area.

Migration waits acquire the appropriate table level lock, recheck for empty or present or non migration content, and sleep with the lock held only while migration is still indicated. Any other observed content causes immediate unlock without sleep.

Table inspection for marker clearing and large swap evaluation and protection fault resolution holds the table lock across live entry comparison against the fault snapshot. Mismatch aborts without modification, while match permits update and cache refresh before unlock.
Balancing restoration modifies protections through a start and commit pairing that preserves atomicity for concurrent table walkers, followed by a cache update covering the modified span.

Marker fault handling prioritizes corruption handling over write protection handling. Poisoned and guard and unknown values terminate, empty values terminate as unexpected, and write protection markers either dissolve when disarmed or continue along the missing entry path when armed.

Fault accounting ignores incomplete faults awaiting retry. General fault counters include both successful and failed faults, while error outcomes stop before per task and performance accounting. A successful fault counts as major when marked major or previously attempted, otherwise minor, and faults without register context skip performance events.

Least recently used fault tracking has a recording configuration and a silent configuration. The recording form stores area recency in current task state on entry and clears it on exit, while the silent form performs no tracking on either boundary.

Empty markers and unknown markers and guard markers all terminate the faulting context, with poisoning reported as hardware poisoning. Inconsistent flag combinations and unexpected writability or reference counts trigger developer warnings rather than silent correction.

Distinct marker categories for poisoning and guard pages and userfault write protection, and distinct fault outcomes for bus error and segmentation violation and hardware poisoning and retry and major or minor success, form part of the observable fault interface.

Distinct direction and mode flags for write and unshare and remote access and force and pinning and long term use, and distinct area capabilities for read and write and shared and locked and growing, form part of the observable memory interface.

A userfault write protection marker without current arming in the area is eligible for conversion to an empty entry, while an armed area follows the missing entry path. Conversion applies only to that exact marker value observed under protection.
